comment: War (GDD 9.3; stage 4e, ADR 0021, decisions of 2026-11-07). Every war has a goal: land (a settlement of the enemy, named when war is declared), loot (the enemy's stores) or revenge (needs a cause: an attack, an aggression or a settlement of ours they hold). goals: victimPercent and witnessPercent say how strongly the victim and everyone who knows both sides remember the aggression (relations.json aggression). Score runs from -100 to 100: a fight won gives the winner's side scorePerWin, a settlement taken scorePerSettlement more. Fighting happens in campaigns (ADR 0022: episodes with a step of campaignStepMonths): warriors of one settlement (at most sendPercent of them, at least minWarriors; a third stays home) march as an army unit (units.json: the best army kind they know, warriors 15 ticks per flat cell, stage 6 PR 3b) over the cheapest known way to an enemy settlement, stand within their kind's range of it and fight there a month of action later (unless their commander calls them back: ai.json commander), take what they can carry and go home. An army sees the settlements at most armySightCells cells from where it stands. Wars end by themselves in time: the world clock takes a step in the month a quiet war runs out. A war in which nobody campaigned for quietPeaceYears ends in a white peace. Weariness of a side (0..100) = months of campaigning in the war x wearinessPerCampaignMonth + percent of the side's people killed in the war x wearinessPerLossPercent; at peaceAbove the side looks for peace at once; it lowers the mood of every settlement of the side by moodAtFullWeariness at 100 (effect war_weariness in effects.json). Peace terms: when the score is at least termsAboveScore, the loser hands over the settlement a war for land was about, or else pays a one-time ransom of ransomPercentPerScorePoint percent of every store per score point from termsAboveScore up (at most maxRansomPercent); a closer war ends in a white peace. cedeWorth: what a settlement handed over is worth in score points when a side weighs terms. Arms (stage 4e PR 3, decision of 2026-11-07): armaments are the levels of arms; every warrior takes the strongest level whose technology the civilization knows and whose good (perWarrior units for one campaign, used up when the warriors set out) the settlement still has; one level needs neither (bare hands). strengthPercent: strength of a warrior with it (stone-tipped spears = 100). Defenders fight with the arms their stores allow without using them up; everyone else in a defended settlement fights bare-handed. Armies (PR 3): warriors of every own settlement at most musterCells cells from the settlement the campaign leaves from may join it (each sends at most sendPercent of its warriors); they gather there first (the muster takes the months the farthest needs to walk). An army has at most armyLimit warriors and stands on one cell per troopsPerCell warriors (eras.json; in eras 1-2 both 50, so one cell). supply: a warrior eats foodPerWarriorPerYear; a campaign sets out with food for carryFoodMonths months (36 since stage 6 PR 3b: a march of 15 cells takes about 45 months of action), at most what its warriors carry and at most supplySharePercent of each settlement's food. While it gathers at home it eats from the home settlement's stores. When it has food for fewer than convoyBelowMonths months, the own settlement at most carrierCells cells away that can send the most food sends carriers (at most carriersPercent of its people who do not fight, each carrying carrying.perPerson of settlements.json, at most supplySharePercent of its food); they walk as a unit of carriers (units.json) after the army and go home when they hand over the food. A hungry campaign (no food left, loot eaten too) loses hungerMoralePerMonth morale a month, a fed one wins back fedMoralePerMonth; strength in a fight is multiplied by morale (percent); below retreatMorale it turns back; while hungry it raids the nearest known settlement of the enemy at most forageCells cells away for food and then marches on. A hungry campaign takes food first when it raids, and does not raid the same settlement twice in a row. Battles (stage 4e PR 4): a campaign that attacks fights a battle of at most battle.rounds rounds (stream combat). Strength of a side = armed strength (arms, see above) times morale; the attackers' times hungryStrengthPercent when they have no food left; the defenders' raised by the terrain of their settlement's cell (terrain: hills, mountains, a river on the edge the attackers come over, the listed biomes; percents add up). Defenders are the warriors and defenderNonWarriorPercent of everyone else (population.json); they start with defenderMorale. In every round each side kills strength x casualtyPercent / 100 men (100 = one warrior with stone-tipped spears), times its luck of the round drawn from rollPercent, the fraction of a man by chance; every percent of its men lost costs a side moralePerLossPercent morale; a side whose morale falls below breakMorale breaks (both: the one with less morale) and loses routLossPercent of its remaining men while fleeing. When nobody breaks within the rounds, the defenders hold. Defenders who die are warriors first. Won: a village the war for land is about passes to the winner with its people; the people of a defeated camp flee to their nearest settlement with what they can carry and the camp is left; otherwise the winners plunder. Working values, to be tuned in stage 4e PR 6. Since stage 6 PR 3b armies walk about 9 times slower than before (3 months of action per flat cell instead of a third), so the values per month of a campaign were scaled down: carryFoodMonths 3 to 36, convoyBelowMonths 3 to 18, hungerMoralePerMonth 20 to 3, fedMoralePerMonth 10 to 2, wearinessPerCampaignMonth 5 to 0.6. Warriors who came home rest restMonths months of action before their settlement can send them again; an army beaten in battle flees home and nobody can turn it (stage 6 PR 3b, decision of 2026-11-09). Since stage 6 PR 2 (decision of 2026-11-09) durations of war, diplomacy and politics are years of action: one year = 12 months of action = 60 ticks = 6 s at x1 (time.json).
